the dermis is regenerated by the stump of the root sheath, which is the dermal component of the hair follicle.
dermal neoformation during skin wound healing proceeds from the stump of fibrous root sheaths of the transected follicles and the epidermis of the epithelization unit.

the development and healing of partial thickness wounds.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
dermal neoformation proceeds by a process of dermal papillary formation from the stump of fibrous root sheaths.

partial thickness wounds heal by a complex and dynamic process that is characterized by the development of an epithelialization unit that advances in a wave-like fashion from the hair follicles and that is coupled with the development of a dermal papillary network.
the dermal neoformative process in the partial thickness skin wound is the development of papillary dermis and that it is the result of the epithelialization process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the healing of full thickness skin wound proceeds by the epithelialization unit, and the healing of partial thickness skin wound proceeds from the stump of fibrous root sheaths.

the dermal neo-formation process in partial and full thickness wounds is the same, and the development of the dermal papillae in both wounds proceeds from the stump of fibrous root sheaths and is coupled with advancing epidermal epithelization from the hair follicle.
the dermal papilla and the fibrous root are the two most important structures for the dermal neo-formation process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the epithelium is the key player in skin wound healing.

the dermal neo-formation process proceeds from the stump of fibrous root sheaths of hair follicles and that the development of a papillary dermis occurs as the epidermal layer advances from the hair follicle.

the epithelialization process is a complex, dynamic and highly organized phenomenon that involves the coordinated action of multiple cell types, including the epidermal keratinocytes, the dermal fibroblasts and the hair follicles.
